root_cause: In rich/pretty.py traverse(), the dataclass branch iterates `fields(obj) if field.repr` and calls `getattr(obj, field.name)` unconditionally. A dataclass field declared with `field(init=False)` and no default is never set on the instance, so getattr raises AttributeError and console.print / pretty_repr crashes.
best_solution: Read 'missing field in dataclass' literally: a field that fields() declares but the instance does not have. Reproduce with `@dataclass(eq=False) class C: item: int = field(init=False)`, then `Console().print(C())`, which raises AttributeError at pretty.py getattr(obj, field.name). Fix: extend the field filter to `if field.repr and hasattr(obj, field.name)`, so missing attributes are skipped. The node already has empty=f"{cls}()", so a dataclass with no present fields renders as `C()`. One generator-expression change, no new API.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_pretty.py::test_dataclass_no_attribute: a @dataclass(eq=False) with `item: int = field(init=False)`, instantiated without setting item; console.print inside console.capture() must not raise, and the output must equal exactly 'BadDataclass()\n' (the missing field is silently omitted, not shown as an error or placeholder).
locating_signals: The title says only 'missing field in dataclass' plus an issue link (issue text not included). 'dataclass' plus rich's printing leads to rich/pretty.py traverse(), where the only dataclass field loop is `for last, field in loop_last(field for field in fields(obj) if field.repr)`. No function is named. The decisive clue is the crash, which you only find by building an instance that lacks a declared attribute (init=False, no default).
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass=false); the hidden test fails with AttributeError: 'BadDataclass' object has no attribute 'item' at rich/pretty.py:786. Every config read 'missing field' as a display problem with repr=False fields, not a crash on an absent attribute. v4 (295s, 102 calls) changed no source at all and left about 15 scratch repro scripts (test_dataclass_repr_false_*.py, test_node*.py) at the repo root. v6 added `empty=f"{cls}()"` to the attrs Node (the wrong branch; the dataclass branch already had it) and left repro files. v7 added an unused `is_dataclass: bool` field to the Node dataclass, which does nothing. v8 produced an empty patch. None tried an init=False field, so none hit the getattr crash.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a short PR title plus an issue link you cannot read, turn each noun phrase into a concrete runtime failure before you edit. 'Missing X' usually means X is declared but absent at runtime (an AttributeError or KeyError), not that X is hidden in the output. Write a 3-line repro that raises. Then harden the introspection loop, e.g. skip it with hasattr or use getattr(obj, name, sentinel), rather than adding flags or changing formatting. If your repro does not crash or change behavior on the base commit, you have the wrong reading, so try the next one (init=False, a del'd attribute, __slots__ without a value) before you stop. Never submit only scratch files.
